step_findings.independent_assessment: The common-right-multiple relation is reflexive/symmetric. Its transitivity uses ve=pf to refine the two middle t-denominator coefficients, producing s u e=w q f and m u e=l q f. All products used as denominators stay nonzero in a domain. No cancellation in M is used.

Independence of addition follows by refining w and w-prime and canceling the nonzero ring denominators s,t, not module elements. For an input refinement (m,s)->(ma,sa), a common refinement gives u c=a u-prime c-prime and v c=v-prime c-prime, hence equal numerator sums. Finite common denominator computation supplies the additive group laws.

For w=su=tv, s-inverse=u w-inverse and t-inverse=v w-inverse in the correct noncommutative order. Equality a s-inverse=b t-inverse implies au=bv after multiplication by w on the RIGHT. Embedding R in K makes this an equality in R, giving beta independence.

Beta is biadditive and R-balanced using beta(mr,a s-inverse)=[mra,s]=beta(m,ra s-inverse). The explicit generators-and-relations universal map exists without choosing a presentation for every k. The inverse composites check on all fractions and elementary tensors. Right K multiplication respects additivity and balancing, with order (m tensor k)ell=m tensor k ell.

The exact quotient equivalence with [0,1] gives a nonzero right annihilator of m. Conversely ma=0 makes denominator sa a common right multiple of s and1. Thus the denominator-independent zero criterion, torsion kernel and module-vanishing criterion all hold for arbitrary right modules. No uniform annihilator is claimed.

Localization of an injection is injective by f(ma)=0; a surjection lifts only the numerator of a fixed fraction. Exactness at M follows from g(m)a=0, then ma=f(p), and [m,s]=[ma,sa]. This proves exactness rather than importing tensor-flatness or a projective-resolution theorem. All witnesses are chosen for the fixed assertion only.

Apply exactness to the cycle inclusion, image factorization and boundary inclusion in each degree. The resulting quotient is H_i(C) tensor K and the canonical map sends [z] tensor k to [z tensor k]. These operations are natural in chain maps. No totalization, infinite product, boundedness or finite generation is used.

Left Ore gives t a=b s and a s-inverse=t-inverse b, with t,b nonzero when a is nonzero. In the opposite ring this is a right fraction. The swap m tensor k -> k tensor m is balanced: (r m) tensor k and m tensor k r correspond to k tensor r m and k r tensor m. Right K-op multiplication becomes the specified left K action. This yields right flatness, left-annihilator detection and left-module homology with correct order.
